analysis: The PR changes only two XCTest/Swift Testing suite declarations. GLM5NextTensorParallelPrefixRestoreTests.swift line 27 adds the `.boundedBufferCache` trait. GLM5NextTensorParallelSpeculationRowsTests.swift line 15 adds `.boundedBufferCache(gib: 4)`. No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache-storage logic is modified. Test bodies are identical between base and head; the full-file head text for the restore tests matches the base apart from line 27. The trait definition itself is not in the supplied evidence (it is presumably a test-support helper defined elsewhere), so its effect, such as setting MLX buffer cache limits and restoring them afterwards, is unverified. It is test-only and most plausibly reduces memory pressure in the opt-in GPU tests. The restore tests exercise the encrypted SSD prefix tier (related to T-041) with a fixed test key (0x2c repeated) under a temporary directory. That is test-fixture material, not a production secret, and the PR does not alter it. The tests write to FileManager.temporaryDirectory and clean up with defer. I found no new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumptions. Remaining question for integration: confirm that the `boundedBufferCache` trait is defined in test targets only and does not ship in production binaries. This does not affect the security conclusion.
